requirement:
A closed `:::{cite} full.name` fence in the book, outside a requirement or
example declaration, opts its explanatory passage into citation review.
A passage needs a review when it contains at least one resolved citation
other than `habeas:util`.

The outermost eligible citation fence identifies the passage. Its opening
citation and citations throughout its body belong to one review, including
citations inside nested commentary containers. References inside nested
requirement or example declarations belong to those declarations' assessments.

The review's subject is the enclosing citation fence's outline node, rather
than the whole chapter. Its inputs include the passage and each cited
declaration or built-in text, with the terminology they use. For project
requirements and examples, the reviewer checks that the passage's claims agree
with and are supported by the cited declarations. Contradicting or unsupported
claims produce a negative assessment. Built-in citations retain their
permitted-role and stated-criteria checks under
{cite}`requirements.references.citation_review`.

These passages use the citation-review storage, freshness checks, selection,
and `author --all` workflow of {cite}`requirements.references.citation_review`.
Their identities follow the existing outline-selector rules. Rendering follows
{cite}`requirements.references.book_badges`. Unfenced book citations retain
their existing behavior.
rationale:
The four marked tests cover every obligation of `requirements.references.citation_review.book_commentary` that this requirement itself carries. Rendering, and the storage, freshness, selection and `author --all` rules, are cited from `requirements.references.citation_review` and `requirements.references.book_badges`. They are reviewed there and need no separate test here. I judged the tests against the requirement text and did not read the implementation.

**Eligibility of passages**
- `src/citations.rs#mod[tests]/fn[book_commentary_groups_nested_citations_but_excludes_declarations_and_literals]` builds one chapter containing many cases. It asserts exactly one book item for `md/notes.md`, with `ReviewKind::BookCommentary`. That item comes from the outer fence, which has a `habeas:util` opening and other resolved citations. These cases produce no items:
  - an unfenced inline citation;
  - a `habeas:util`-only fence;
  - a fence citing an unresolved name;
  - a cite fence inside a `{req}` declaration;
  - a fence inside a code block;
  - an unclosed fence.
- `src/citations.rs#mod[tests]/fn[separate_closed_passages_have_independent_subjects_and_empty_book_cites_stay_exempt]` covers three further cases. A fence inside raw HTML is a literal and gives no review. A chapter with only an inline citation gives no item. Two separate closed fences give two items with different `item` selectors and different `review_path()` values.

**Outermost fence, grouping and subject**
- In the first citations test, the exact citation list is `habeas:util`, `requirements.ready`, `requirements.ready`, `notes.nested`, `notes.illustration`, `habeas:coverage`. This shows that the outer opening citation, the nested cite fence's opening and the body citations after the nested containers are all included. It also shows that references inside the nested `{req}` and `{example}` are excluded.
- The same test resolves the item's outline node. It is a `block` that starts with the outer fence and contains the "Outer passage" and "Nested passage" text. It excludes the unfenced prose and the utility-only passage. This checks that the subject is the fence node rather than the whole chapter.
- A fence in a non-book file stays `ReviewKind::SourceItem`.

**Inputs, prompt and assessment**
- `src/authoring/mod.rs#mod[tests]/fn[book_commentary_reviews_supply_the_whole_passage_and_check_concordance]` checks the mandatory inputs. `mandatory[0]` is the passage's file and item, and the inputs include `requirements.ready` and the terminology definition `terms.unit`.
- The same test checks that the prompt:
  - has the book_commentary review kind;
  - contains the passage text, the cited requirement's text and the term text;
  - states "Contradicting or unsupported claims are gaps";
  - does not contain unrelated or adjacent chapter prose.
- A false judgment after a contradicting edit ("seconds" versus the unit definition) is recorded with `determination` false. `validate_review` then reports "determination is false", so a negative assessment is enforced.

**Freshness and identity**
- After the passage text changes, validation reports a hash error. Removing the opt-in fence reports an "orphaned citation review".
- `src/authoring/batch.rs#mod[tests]/fn[book_passages_are_selected_refreshed_skipped_and_removed_with_citation_reviews]` covers the batch workflow. A current review is skipped and counted as unchanged. A forced selection re-includes it. A text change re-selects it. Removing the fence makes `subject_is_current` false, and `delete_orphaned_reviews` deletes the review file.

**Residual points**
- The built-in text input and the permitted-role checks for built-ins in a book passage are not asserted in the book-specific tests. The requirement delegates them to `requirements.references.citation_review`. The shared input path is covered elsewhere, for example by `src/authoring/inputs.rs#mod[tests]/fn[citation_review_inputs_combine_item_declarations_terms_and_built_ins_once]`.
- Nested commentary containers other than cite fences, `{req}` and `{example}` are not exercised. A nested cite fence is, and it behaves as the requirement describes.

I found no requirement-violating behavior that these tests would accept.

A closed `:::{cite} full.name` fence in the book, outside a requirement or
example declaration, opts its explanatory passage into citation review.
A passage needs a review when it contains at least one resolved citation
other than `habeas:util`.
The outermost eligible citation fence identifies the passage. Its opening
citation and citations throughout its body belong to one review, including
citations inside nested commentary containers. References inside nested
requirement or example declarations belong to those declarations' assessments.
The review's subject is the enclosing citation fence's outline node, rather
than the whole chapter. Its inputs include the passage and each cited
declaration or built-in text, with the terminology they use. For project
requirements and examples, the reviewer checks that the passage's claims agree
with and are supported by the cited declarations. Contradicting or unsupported
claims produce a negative assessment. Built-in citations retain their
permitted-role and stated-criteria checks under
{cite}`requirements.references.citation_review`.
These passages use the citation-review storage, freshness checks, selection,
and `author --all` workflow of {cite}`requirements.references.citation_review`.
Their identities follow the existing outline-selector rules. Rendering follows
{cite}`requirements.references.book_badges`. Unfenced book citations retain
their existing behavior.
:::{req} citation_review
Every source item outside the book that carries at least one `{cite}` reference
other than a citation of `habeas:util` under {cite}`requirements.references.util`
MUST have a citation review: an assessment of that item's citations, recorded at
`evidence/citations/<file>/<selector>.json`, where `<file>` is the item's
project-relative path, `<selector>` is its outline selector with every `/` and
`%` percent-encoded, and the root node uses `_root`. The review MUST use the
prompt defined by {cite}`requirements.authoring.citation_prompt`. For citations
of project requirements and examples, the reviewer MUST assess whether the item
should be re-checked or kept in sync when the cited definition changes, and
whether the reference procedure of
{cite}`requirements.references.procedure` calls for `{impl}` or `{test}` instead.
For citations of built-ins, the reviewer MUST check the permitted reference
roles and forms and any citation-review criteria stated in the built-in's fixed
text, using the item's source and commentary. A permitted citation role alone
MUST NOT suffice when the fixed text states additional criteria. Mandatory inputs,
under {cite}`requirements.authoring.mandatory_inputs`, MUST be the item's outline
node, each cited declaration or built-in text, and the citations' commentary. The record MUST contain the item's file and selector,
its citations by role, name, and commentary, `determination`, `rationale`, and
`inputs`, with determinations under {cite}`requirements.ci.outcomes`. Validation
MUST require a current, accepted review for every such item and report stale,
missing, or orphaned reviews; a review MUST become stale when the item's hash,
a cited declaration, or its citations or their commentary change. Authoring with
`--all` MUST include citation reviews, and `habeas author citations:<file>#<selector>`
MUST author the review of the one item it names, under
{cite}`requirements.authoring.refresh`, where omitting `#<selector>`
names the file's root node. A citation in a requirement or example
declaration is reviewed as part of that definition's own assessment instead.
Fenced commentary elsewhere in the book is reviewed under
{cite}`requirements.references.citation_review.book_commentary`.
Storage MAY use the versioned representation under
{cite}`requirements.sdk.habeas.evidence_format`, retaining the same review
information and validation rules.
:::{req} book_badges
In a book chapter, each valid `{impl}`, `{cite}`, or `{test}` reference, inline
or fenced, renders as a Shields.io static badge image, subject to the
citation-only paragraph exception below and the reviewed-passage display under
{cite}`requirements.references.citation_review.book_commentary.display`.
The badge has meaningful alt text displaying its role and full name, and links
to the badge at the corresponding `{req}` or `{example}` definition. Links
work across chapters, including nested chapters. Apart from the reviewed-passage
exception, a fenced reference renders its badge followed by its body as Markdown.
Inside any prose-bearing colon-fenced section, top-level paragraphs containing
one or more valid inline `{cite}` references and otherwise only whitespace are
omitted from the chapter. This applies to requirements, examples, definitions,
reference fences, and other prose containers, including nested sections.
Requirement and example detail pages still render those citations.
Citations within explanatory prose, lists or blockquotes, unfenced chapter
prose, and references of other roles retain their usual rendering.
Escaped roles, code, raw HTML, and unresolvable references remain literal.
The original declaration, reference discovery, and authoring inputs retain the
citations.
Each fenced `{req}` or `{example}` directive renders with a badge identifying
its kind and full name; text outside a directive remains literal. Declaration
badge navigation follows {cite}`requirements.index.navigation`.
Badge text remains legible regardless of whether its link has been visited.
A badge link shows a visible indicator when it has keyboard focus and may
brighten on hover. Badges may be laid out inline with the surrounding text, a
fenced reference's badge and body may be visually set apart from the surrounding
text as one block, and a built-in's unlinked badge may show a help cursor to
signal its hover text. These badges use the syntax defined by
{cite}`requirements.references.roles`.
